key_insight: Detonation-sprayed AlB12–Al coatings on 45 steel deliver high hardness and notably improved wear resistance, with the AlB12–30 wt.% Al composition showing the most stable tribological behavior.
engineering_relevance: The results support AlB12–Al detonation coatings as a practical surface-engineering route for extending steel component life under friction and wear.
method: Applied AlB12–30 wt.% Al (AB70) and AlB12–70 wt.% Al (AB30) detonation coatings onto 45 steel using the DNEPR-5M system.
Evaluated coating thickness, microhardness, hardness, friction coefficient, and wear rate under different sliding speeds and loads.
Compared worn-surface structure and wear mechanisms after testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coating thickness of about 170–200 μm, μH = 27–29 GPa, HV = 4.35 GPa, and for AB70 a friction coefficient of 0.21–0.38 with wear rate of 3.3–8.6 μm/km, outperforming uncoated 45 steel.
watch_item: Wear behavior varies with friction mode, and the observed oxidative versus adhesive-abrasive mechanisms suggest performance will depend strongly on service conditions.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
